response_text: Yes, the OS will still work. The way the osSched works is through taking the incrementation of the index in the thread array and then the modulus of the number of threads. This implements a round robin scheduling of the threads. Each thread will run one after the other, and the overall cycle will wrap into a circle. If there is only one thread, there will only be one step in the cycle, meaning that it will just come back to itself and continue to run. In terms of reality, this makes sense. There may be scenarios where is only one thread that is being run and there are no other threads to be run.\n
